title: Police seek witnesses to deadly shooting
article: The Special Investigations Unit is appealing to anyone who witnessed the shooting of a man by police officers in downtown Bradford Sunday to come forward.
South Simcoe Police were searching for 38-year-old Mark Norman Graham in connection with a shooting that took place outside the Trophy Case Tavern in Bradford early Sunday morning.
Police, with the help of the Emergency Response and Canine units, tracked him down at around 2:30 p.m. Sunday near the Tim Hortons restaurant on Holland Street.
Witnesses say that Graham walked defiantly away from police and was subsequently gunned down and killed.
The SIU has dispatched eight investigators, including three forensic identification technicians, to comb the scene for details.
The SIU is currently interviewing one witness officer.
Rose Hong, communications officer for the SIU, said there are two subject officers identified so far. The subject officers are not obligated to speak if they choose not to, she says.
"Right now investigators in Bradford are canvassing the area for civilian witnesses who may have seen the shooting," says Hong.
The SIU is called in circumstances where there is serious inju, or death, involving a police officer and a civilian.
It is within the jurisdiction of the SIU to lay criminal charges when it can objectively establish through evidence that a crime has taken place, says Hong.
In the first incident, police say that Graham and the victim, who were acquaintances, became involved in a dispute outside the tavern when the shooting occurred.
The victim is currently in critical condition.
A post-mortem will conducted on Graham Tuesday to determine the official cause of death, says Hong.
Police are not releasing any more details at this time.
